suggestions.assertion: Automatic checks: check_doc.py on report.md and every sibling Markdown file reports no Blocker and at most two Majors in total
suggestions.reason: 'Every sibling Markdown file' is ambiguous. The outputs folder also holds user_notes.md and report.data/upgrade-notes.md. Run on them, user_notes.md gives a Blocker (B4 'unbalanced details': a false positive, because check_doc.py counts the literal tag inside inline code on lines 19 and 39) and the unedited input copy gives two Majors (B1, C1), which an input file can never avoid. Name the files in scope (report.md and report.*.md) and make the checker skip inline-code spans.

suggestions.assertion: A1 Zones marked and ordered: ... heading or banner names its audience (a pointer line in the header does not count) ...
suggestions.reason: The skeleton's own heading '## [person glyph] START HERE - at a glance' does not literally name an audience. I passed it because the metadata line says 'for Marcus Hale, Engineering Lead' and the marker reads zone:human, but a stricter grader would fail every output that copies the skeleton. Decide whether the heading itself must name the audience and align the skeleton or the assertion.

suggestions.assertion: B2 Order follows understanding: ... terms are defined before the first section that uses them ...
suggestions.reason: It is unclear whether the glance panel counts as 'the first section that uses' a term. The run uses 'the shim' and 'mixed-version check' in the panel (lines 27, 10) before the section 1 glossary (lines 59, 61). Say whether the glossary must precede the panel's jargon or only the numbered sections.

suggestions.assertion: A3 Machine and archive blocks are collapsed in details blocks ... long material sits in a sibling file behind a pointer
suggestions.reason: The assertion asks for details blocks and for pointers at once. The run satisfied it with two collapsed blocks and two uncollapsed pointer blocks (the executor flagged the same ambiguity). State whether a pointer block needs details.

No assertion checks body-level factual accuracy beyond the two Figures numbers, and I found three small slips: section 1 says a failure in the Identity pair reaches 'seven of the other eight' services (true only for user-store); section 4 calls auth-service and user-store 'the two most critical services' although services.csv also marks gateway critical; the timeline title says v8 support ends 'a week later' than Fri 30 Oct (it is 13 days). Add an assertion such as: every number or ranking in sections 1-5 that restates services.csv or incidents-q3.csv matches the data (spot-check five).

suggestions.assertion: D2 Coverage and truth: ... inferred edges are dashed and captioned
suggestions.reason: Vacuous for this fixture: every dependency edge is in services.csv, so the clause can never be tested. A fixture variant with one dependency mentioned only in the notes would exercise it.

suggestions.assertion: C2 Compact panel: about 300 words of prose or fewer ...
suggestions.reason: Tension with B1: the 7-link reading path takes roughly a third of the budget (292 of 300 words used) and the run shrank each descriptor to 2-3 words such as 'terms, table'. State whether the reading path is excluded from the panel word count or require descriptors of a minimum useful length.

eval_feedback.overall: The assertions are mostly meaningful and this run met all 21 with concrete evidence, but several (A1, A3, B2, F3) hinge on wording that the skeleton itself satisfies verbatim or ambiguously, and no assertion covers body-level factual accuracy, where three small slips went uncaught. Tighten those four wordings, scope the automatic-check files, and add a data-accuracy spot-check.
